bull_bear.body:
- Over five decades of track record (100th Annual Report; incorporated 1926) as a pioneer in the Indian water-supply pipeline and EPC industry
- Presence across nearly all water-supply-related activities - manufacturing, laying, jointing, treatment plants, pumping stations, reservoirs - giving turnkey/end-to-end execution capability
- Long-standing dedicated supplier of concrete railway sleepers to Indian Railways
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competition from medium/large-scale construction entities — Management flagged increased competition from larger construction players as a threat to the Company's water-supply/pipeline construction business.
- Substitution by alternative pipe materials — Availability of substitute pipe materials such as Ductile Iron pipes, spirally welded steel pipes and HDPE pipes is cited as a competitive threat to the Company's own pipe product mix.
- Raw-material price inflation — Prices of key raw materials - steel, steel wires, HT wires and cement - were on an uptrend during the year, which can pressure margins on fixed-price EPC/supply contracts.
- Geopolitical conflict-driven input cost inflation — The West Asia geopolitical conflict (US-Iran) has intensified global energy-market uncertainty and raised crude oil prices, increasing costs of oil, bought-out items and transportation and thereby raising overall project costs.
- Execution/regulatory risk in land-monetization projects — The Wadala (Mumbai) SRA project and the Badarpur (New Delhi) land are still at the initial stage of obtaining development-related approvals; realizing value from these land parcels depends on navigating regulatory frameworks and market dynamics, creating timing/execution uncertainty for this newer segment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures, lays and joints pipelines (RCC, Steel, Prestressed Concrete, Penstock, Bar Wrapped Steel Cylinder, Prestressed Concrete Cylinder) and executes turnkey EPC water-supply, irrigation, sanitation and sewerage projects for Central/State Governments and local bodies across India, including full-system works such as intake wells, treatment plants, pumping stations and reservoirs; it also supplies concrete railway sleepers to Indian Railways. Since FY2023-24 it has added a land-development segment that monetizes the Company's own land parcels via real-estate projects.

business.title: Competitive strengths

outlook.body:
- Diversification into Bar Wrapped Steel Cylinder (BWSC) and Prestressed Concrete Cylinder (PCCP) pipes as alternatives to M.S. and D.I. pipes, with expanded manufacturing footprint through dedicated plants at Choutuppal (Telangana), Chilamathur (Andhra Pradesh), Miraj, Dhule, Walwa and Kanhan (Maharashtra), plus added capability at existing factories at Patancheru, Kekri, Sikar and Karari to meet growing government demand.
- Ongoing monetization of surplus land parcels through real-estate development (Hadapsar and Vadgaon in Pune; Wadala SRA in Mumbai; Badarpur in Delhi) to unlock non-core asset value alongside the core construction business.
- Continued focus on turnkey EPC execution across the full water-supply value chain (source to distribution, including treatment plants, pumping stations and reservoirs) rather than pipe supply alone, sustaining a diversified geographic presence across many Indian states.
- The Board follows a Board-approved Dividend Distribution Policy (applicable under SEBI's mandate for the top 1,000 listed entities by market capitalisation) with a stated philosophy of enhancing long-term shareholder value; the Company has, in addition to a normal annual dividend, recommended special/one-off dividends tied to milestone events (e.g., anniversary, land-sale gains). Corporate governance philosophy emphasises internally driven transparency, accountability and business ethics rather than compliance-only conduct, with liquidity managed to maintain satisfactory optimum utilisation of financial resources and cordial banker/creditor relationships.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Company expanded its BWSC/PCCP (Bar Wrapped Steel Cylinder / Prestressed Concrete Cylinder) pipe manufacturing footprint by specially setting up plants at Choutuppal (Telangana), Chilamathur (Andhra Pradesh), Miraj, Dhule, Walwa and Kanhan (Maharashtra), and by adding BWSC/PCCP manufacturing capability at its existing factories at Patancheru, Kekri, Sikar and Karari, to meet growing demand for these alternative pipe materials from Government authorities. Separately, per the BRSR Principle 2 disclosure, the Company incurred Rs.1,353.12 Lakhs of capex during FY26 (against Rs.5,493.30 Lakhs in FY25) for improving product quality, and Rs.595.06 Lakhs on R&D during FY26 (against Rs.575 Lakhs in FY25) for new product formulation.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Structural, long-term demand for water-supply, irrigation, sanitation and sewerage infrastructure driven by India's water scarcity (over 18% of world population but only 4% of world's renewable water resources) and growing population, per the National Water Policy 2012 framing cited by management.
- Government focus on interlinking rivers is expected to significantly expand lift-irrigation schemes, creating strong demand for water-conveyance pipes; management believes the Company is well-positioned to benefit through increased production and sales of irrigation pipes.
- Rural water-supply demand is expected to increase sharply with State Government development programmes aimed at improving rural economic conditions, alongside rising domestic, industrial, agricultural and power-sector water needs.
- Rising raw-material costs (steel, steel wires, HT wires, cement) amid the West Asia geopolitical conflict and higher crude oil prices are flagged as an inflationary pressure on input costs and overall project costs.
- Increased competition from medium/large-scale construction entities and availability of substitute pipe materials (Ductile Iron pipes, spirally welded steel pipes, HDPE pipes) are cited as a competitive threat.
- Company's works on numerous Water Supply Projects, Drainage Schemes and Irrigation Schemes across Maharashtra, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh and Chhattisgarh are progressing well or nearing completion, including several EPC contracts with attached Operation & Maintenance periods of up to five years.
- During the year, the Company received orders worth Rs.1,396.19 Lakhs for BWSC pipes, Rs.26,736.57 Lakhs for PCCP pipes and Rs.833.27 Lakhs for PSC pipes, in each case along with other civil works.
- Railway Sleepers segment carried a total outstanding order book of Rs.8,282.98 Lakhs as on 31st March, 2025, and during the year received a further work order of Rs.4,321.40 Lakhs from the Ministry of Railways, Railway Board, New Delhi, for manufacture of 1,55,000 sleepers.
